title: The List of 962: Pistoia, Salo, the Lodge, and the Hill Above Arezzo
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Pistoia, and the Schools of Italy

stops.name: Pistoia, birth under the Duomo
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia EN/IT). The pin is Piazza del Duomo, a town-centre point; no source gives a birth address.
stops.campa: In Pistoia, a Tuscan town of stone arcades and small trades, a son is born on the twenty-first of April to a family of no fortune. They name him Licio. The year he is born, a movement forms in Milan that will hold the state before the boy can read about it, and hold it for the whole of his youth. He will bury a brother in Spain, carry three party cards, keep a roll of nine hundred and sixty-two names in a factory safe, and be brought back into this same town, ninety-six years later, to be put in the ground.
suggested_refs: The civil register of Pistoia for April 1919

stops.name: Pistoia, expelled from every school in Italy
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed from his age. IT Wikipedia has him a seventeen-year-old liceo classico student, which places this at c. 1936-37; the date 1930 carried in English summaries is wrong by about six years, since he was ten then. Coordinate is the Liceo Forteguerri, approximate; month and day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: A seventeen-year-old at the liceo classico strikes a teacher across the face. The penalty is not local. He is expelled from every school in the kingdom, a sentence of the whole state pronounced on a boy in a provincial classroom. He does not appeal it and does not go back to study. He is out of the classroom at seventeen, in a country where the liceo classico is the door to the professions, and he never goes through it. The Italian record gives the age and the blow. It does not give the teacher's name, the month, or what he did the following year.
suggested_refs: Liceo Classico Forteguerri, Piazza San Francesco, Pistoia

stops.name: Malaga, the brother and the decoration
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Malaga offensive is February 1937 and the day of Gelli's arrival is not recorded.
stops.campa: He crosses to Spain with the Fascist volunteers sent to Franco and fights in the column that takes Malaga in February. His brother Raffaello is killed in the same campaign. Franco decorates him in person, the youngest recruit in his contingent, and he comes home to Pistoia with a Spanish medal and a grave he cannot visit. Two years later he holds a card in the National Fascist Party. He is seventeen, and this is the first decoration a foreign head of state hangs on him; the second comes from Argentina thirty-seven years later.
suggested_refs: Italian volunteer formations at the Malaga offensive, February 1937

stops.name: Salo, the liaison officer and the last republic
stops.date_confidence: the liaison role is attested at year level (1940) with no posting or city named, an open gap. The RSI adherence is attested; 23 September 1943 is the republic's own foundation date, not a date any source attaches to Gelli personally.
stops.campa: Through the early war he serves as liaison between the Italian government and the Germans; no source names the posting or the city. After the armistice of September the kingdom splits in two, and Gelli goes north with the losing half, into the Italian Social Republic on Lake Garda, alongside Giorgio Almirante, who will lead the postwar neo-fascist party for thirty years. He is twenty-four. Sixty-five years later, on a television stage in Florence, he will still speak about this republic in the present tense, and by then he will have been struck from Freemasonry and sentenced five times by the state that replaced it.
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, televised appearance, Florence, 31 October 2008, per it.wikiquote.org
suggested_refs: The ministries of the Italian Social Republic on Lake Garda, 1943-1945

stops.name: Pistoia, the marriage to Wanda Vannacci
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (IT Wikipedia). No church or venue is named in any reachable source; a cathedral attribution circulating in summaries is unsupported and is dropped, so the pin is the town and not a building.
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of December, with the front cutting Italy in half and his republic four months from collapse, he marries Wanda Vannacci. The marriage outlasts everything else in the life: the fascist state, the mattress trade, the lodge, the courts, the prisons. Her name will be fixed to a hill outside Arezzo, on a villa he does not yet own, and that villa will become the address at which Italian history is searched in March 1981. She dies in 1993. He is laid beside her twenty-two years after that.
suggested_refs: Pistoia marriage registers, December 1944

stops.name: Frosinone, commercial director at Permaflex
stops.date_confidence: attested at year level (IT Wikipedia: commercial director at the Permaflex works of Frosinone in 1956). English summaries giving a salesman's job in Tuscany in 1950 are wrong on role, year and region; month and day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: He goes south into Lazio, to the Permaflex mattress works at Frosinone, a plant in the country the Cassa del Mezzogiorno is paying to industrialise, and becomes its commercial director. He is a seller of beds to a nation rebuilding its bedrooms, and he is good at it. The job puts him in rooms with prefects, bankers, and the men who award public contracts in a region where every contract is political. It is the first trade of his life that requires him to be liked by people who can sign things.
suggested_refs: The Permaflex plant at Frosinone and the Cassa del Mezzogiorno industrial programme

stops.name: Rome, initiation in the lodge Gian Domenico Romagnosi
stops.date_confidence: date and lodge attested (EN Wikipedia, 'Propaganda Due'). Palazzo Giustiniani, the Grand Orient's seat, is an inference: no source names the room. Pin approximate, longitude corrected from a point c. 180 m off.
stops.campa: On the sixth of November he is initiated into Freemasonry in Rome, in the lodge Gian Domenico Romagnosi, under the Grande Oriente d'Italia. He is forty-four, a mattress man with a fascist war record and no visible prospects in the republic that outlawed his party. The Grand Orient is a respectable body of professionals and civil servants that meets in a palazzo near the Senate. Seven years from tonight it will hand him a dormant lodge with a number and almost no members, and within a decade the state will be asking whether that lodge governs it.
suggested_refs: Palazzo Giustiniani, Rome, seat of the Grande Oriente d'Italia

stops.name: Rome, Propaganda Due handed over
stops.date_confidence: attested at year level (Wikipedia, 'Propaganda Due'); month and day unknown, defaulted. Pin is the canonical Rome point.
stops.campa: The Grande Oriente d'Italia gives him a lodge that barely exists: Propaganda Due, numbered heir of the lodge of the Risorgimento, reduced to a register and a name. His commission is to reorganise it. He reorganises it by inverting it. Members are recruited one at a time and know only him; the roll is kept by him alone; the lodge holds no meeting a lodge would recognise. Within five years it is not a Masonic body at all but a private list of the officers of the Italian state, held by a man the state has never elected to anything.
stops.quote: limitare il diritto di sciopero alle causali economiche ed assicurare comunque la libertà di lavoro
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, 'Piano di rinascita democratica', quoted in Wikipedia (IT) after the Anselmi parliamentary commission of inquiry
suggested_refs: The register of Propaganda Due before 1970, in the archives of the Grande Oriente d'Italia

stops.name: Rome, the Quirinal and the Golpe Borghese
stops.date_confidence: the coup attempt of 7-8 December 1970 is attested. Gelli's assigned role in it is recorded by IT Wikipedia as non confermato and is carried here as reconstruction, not fact. Quirinal coordinate corrected from a point c. 340 m west.
stops.campa: On the night of the seventh of December, Junio Valerio Borghese, the Black Prince of the Decima MAS, launches a coup that holds the armoury of the Interior Ministry for a few hours and then dissolves before dawn. In the accounts that follow, Gelli is given the arrest of President Giuseppe Saragat at the Quirinal. Italian sources record that role as unconfirmed, and he is never tried for it. What is not in dispute is that in the same year, in the same city, the Grand Orient hands him the lodge.
suggested_refs: The Quirinal Palace, seat of the President of the Italian Republic

stops.name: Rome, Jose Lopez Rega received into the lodge
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level via jose_lopez_rega.journey.json, whose stop is titled 'Rome, the lodge of Licio Gelli'; day unknown, defaulted. Canonical Rome pin inherited byte-identical.
stops.campa: Juan Peron's private secretary comes to Rome in February and is received into Propaganda Due. Jose Lopez Rega has spent seven years making himself indispensable in a villa at Puerta de Hierro; in three months he will be a minister of the Argentine state, and inside two years he will be running the Triple A. The lodge he joins is explicitly Gelli's, worked from an Italian address by a man who holds no office. Argentina and Italy are now joined by a membership roll that neither parliament can read.
suggested_refs: The P2 induction records for February 1973

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Casa Rosada
stops.date_confidence: the swearing-in is attested to the day via jose_lopez_rega.journey.json; pin inherited byte-identical. Gelli's advisory role to the Peronist government and the Libya-Italy-Argentina oil and arms brokerage are reconstruction: they are not in the Wikipedia article usually cited for them, and the framing of Gelli as a fugitive in the 1970s is anachronistic, since he does not become one until 1981.
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of May, Lopez Rega is sworn in as Minister of Social Welfare in the Casa Rosada, ninety days after his induction in Rome. Gelli is not in the building and does not need to be. Later accounts make him an economic adviser to the Peronist government and a broker of oil and arms between Libya, Italy and Argentina; those accounts are carried by no source reachable here, and the article they are usually credited to does not contain them. What is documented is the lodge, the minister, and the ninety days between.
suggested_refs: The Casa Rosada, Buenos Aires, and the ministerial oath of 25 May 1973

stops.name: Madrid, Puerta de Hierro
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The only source is Gelli's own statement, which gives June 1973; nothing corroborates it. Pin inherited byte-identical from jose_lopez_rega.journey.json.
stops.campa: In the exiled Peron's household on the western edge of Madrid, weeks before the old general goes home to be president a third time, Gelli says he initiated him into Freemasonry. He gives the month, the city and the house. The house is the one in which Lopez Rega made himself indispensable, and the one Peron's coffin will later pass out of. Nothing in the Argentine record confirms the initiation, and nothing in Gelli's telling of it ever wavers, across thirty years of interviews.
stops.quote: Peron was a Mason, I initiated him in Madrid in Puerta de Hierro, in June 1973.
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Licio Gelli'; the page names no original publication for the line
suggested_refs: The Peron residence at Puerta de Hierro, Madrid, 1960-1973

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Gran Cruz at the Palacio San Martin
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Reported in biographical summaries with no Argentine decree cited; August 1974 is the date those summaries give and no primary text was located. Day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: Peron is two months dead and Isabel governs. At the Chancellery on the Plaza San Martin the Argentine foreign minister Alberto Vignes hangs on Gelli the Gran Cruz de la Orden del Libertador, the republic's highest decoration for a foreigner, awarded for services no document names. The decoration makes him on paper a friend of the Argentine state, an Italian with a standing in Buenos Aires that no Italian office gives him. When Italy comes for him nine years later, he goes to South America.
suggested_refs: Palacio San Martin, Buenos Aires, seat of the Argentine foreign ministry
sources: Wikipedia, 'Licio Gelli' (award reported, no decree located)

stops.name: Rome, Venerable Master, and the plan
stops.date_confidence: attested at year level (Wikipedia, 'Propaganda Due'); month and day unknown, defaulted. The Piano di rinascita democratica is undated in the reachable sources and is known from the copy seized in 1982.
stops.campa: He becomes Venerable Master of Propaganda Due and takes it out of Masonry altogether. The roll grows to hold generals, prefects, magistrates, editors, bankers, and the heads of all three Italian secret services. He writes a programme for it, the Piano di rinascita democratica, a plan for rebuilding the republic by men who hold no elective office: courts brought under the executive, parties reduced to two, parliament shrunk, provinces abolished, the press acquired, the universities made into private foundations. It is found seven years later in a suitcase.
stops.quote: …rivitalizzare il sistema attraverso la sollecitazione di tutti gli istituti che la Costituzione prevede e disciplina, dagli organi dello Stato ai partiti politici, alla stampa, ai sindacati, ai cittadini elettori
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, 'Piano di rinascita democratica', quoted in Wikipedia (IT) after the Anselmi parliamentary commission of inquiry
suggested_refs: The text of the Piano di rinascita democratica as printed in the Anselmi commission's proceedings

segments.name: The Bank and the Bank of the Pope

stops.name: Milan, Largo Bortolo Belotti
stops.date_confidence: Calvi general manager 1971 and chairman 1975, both attested at year level (Wikipedia, 'Roberto Calvi'); month and day unknown, defaulted. Pin is the Largo Bortolo Belotti headquarters address given by EN Wikipedia, adjacent to the Via Clerici point carried in some summaries.
stops.campa: Roberto Calvi becomes general manager of Banco Ambrosiano, the Catholic bank of Milan, and by 1975 its chairman. He is a member of the lodge. The bank owns newspapers and publishing houses, and its credit reaches into the politics of two continents through a chain of subsidiaries no Italian regulator can follow. Italians call Calvi God's Banker. What the phrase means in practice is that the Vatican holds shares in the offshore companies through which the money leaves, and that the bank has two sets of owners, one of them a lodge.
stops.quote: Il vero potere risiede nelle mani dei detentori dei Mass Media.
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, quoted in Mario Guarino and Fedora Raugei, 'Gli anni del disonore' (2006), via it.wikiquote.org
suggested_refs: The Banco Ambrosiano headquarters at Largo Bortolo Belotti, Milan

stops.name: Lugano, the Banco del Gottardo
stops.date_confidence: the shareholding is attested for the period 1963-1982 (Wikipedia, 'Banco Ambrosiano') without a year of acquisition; 1975 is placed here as the midpoint of the Calvi chairmanship and is not a documented date.
stops.campa: Forty-five percent of the Banco del Gottardo on the Piazza della Riforma is held through Banco Ambrosiano's Luxembourg company. Lugano is an hour from Milan and in another country. Money leaves Italy as a loan to a subsidiary, becomes a deposit in Switzerland, comes back as foreign investment in Italian shares, and by the time it lands the bank owns itself. In 1981 Calvi is convicted of illegal export of currency, fined heavily, given a suspended sentence, and released. The structure survives his conviction by nine months.
suggested_refs: Banco del Gottardo, Piazza della Riforma, Lugano

stops.name: Vatican City, the Institute for Religious Works
stops.date_confidence: the IOR relationship spans the 1970s to 1984; 1980 is a placed year within that span and is not a documented date. The 1984 payment of 224 million dollars is attested (Wikipedia, 'Roberto Calvi').
stops.campa: Behind the walls, the Istituto per le Opere di Religione is run by Archbishop Paul Marcinkus of Cicero, Illinois, who sits on the board of Ambrosiano's Nassau subsidiary and signs letters of comfort acknowledging the Vatican's ownership of the Panamanian shells that hold the debt. The Vatican is a sovereign state. Its bank cannot be subpoenaed by Italy and its officers cannot be arrested inside it. In 1984 it pays two hundred and twenty-four million dollars to the creditors while admitting no liability, only moral involvement.
suggested_refs: The letters of comfort of 1981 signed for the IOR by Paul Marcinkus

stops.name: Bologna Centrale, the second-class waiting room
stops.date_confidence: the bombing is attested to the day. Gelli's role as commissioner and financier is not established until the verdicts of 2020, 2022 and 2024; his definitive conviction for sabotaging the investigation dates from 23 November 1995. Nothing here was known to any court in 1980.
stops.campa: On a Saturday morning in August a bomb goes off in the waiting room of Bologna's central station and kills eighty-five people. It is the worst attack in the history of the republic. For fifteen years the investigation is fed false documents and false witnesses, and in 1995 the Court of Cassation sentences Gelli definitively as a promoter of that sabotage. Twenty-seven years after the bomb, other courts will go further and name him as one of the two men who paid for it. None of this is known to any court in 1980.
suggested_refs: The clock of Bologna Centrale, stopped at 10.25, 2 August 1980

stops.name: Washington, the east front of the Capitol
stops.date_confidence: the invitation is attested (Wikipedia, 'Licio Gelli'). 20 January 1981 is the date of the inauguration itself, not a date any source attaches to Gelli's presence; the pin is the ceremony site.
stops.campa: An Italian businessman holding no office and standing for nothing is among the guests invited to the inauguration of Ronald Reagan. He is Venerable Master of a lodge whose roll no one outside it has read, and he wears the Gran Cruz of a republic now run by its generals. Eight weeks after the ceremony, a tax police search of a textile works outside Arezzo will make his name the most spoken in Italy, and he will not live freely in his own country again for seven years.
suggested_refs: The guest lists of the presidential inauguration of 20 January 1981

stops.name: Castiglion Fibocchi, the roll in the company archive
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, with 962 names and Berlusconi among them. IT Wikipedia's P2 article places the list in the Giole factory archive; other summaries place it in the Arezzo villa, and the disagreement is not resolved here. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from silvio_berlusconi.journey.json; a separate gazetteer point for the comune reads 43.5533, 11.7694.
stops.campa: The Guardia di Finanza, working a lead out of the Michele Sindona investigation, searches the Giole textile works twelve kilometres north-west of Arezzo and opens the company archive. Inside is the roll of Propaganda Due: nine hundred and sixty-two names, among them military officers, prefects, magistrates, editors, bankers, the heads of the three secret services, and a Milanese property developer called Silvio Berlusconi, enrolled in 1978, four years before he owns a national television network. The government falls in May.
stops.quote: Noi con la P2 avevamo l'Italia in mano. Allora c'era l'Esercito, Guardia di Finanza, Polizia: erano nettamente comandate da tutta gente della loggia massonica P2.
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, interview with Klaus Davi, 4 December 2008, per it.wikiquote.org
suggested_refs: The seized P2 membership roll of 962 names, in the records of the Anselmi commission

stops.name: Arezzo, Villa Wanda, gold in the garden
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Coordinate corrected to the villa's own position on the Santa Maria delle Grazie hill (IT Wikipedia gives 43 26 48 N, 11 52 55 E); points c. 2.6 km north in the town centre circulate widely and are wrong. The sources disagree over which of the two searched premises held the membership roll.
stops.campa: The same day, on the hill of Santa Maria delle Grazie above Arezzo, the police search the house. He bought it in 1968 from the Lebole family, who called it Villa Carla, when he took a partnership in their mattress firm, and renamed it for his wife. In the garden they dig up gold ingots. A year earlier a Madonna della Consolazione of 1512, stolen from a sanctuary at Rotonda, had been recovered from the same grounds. The Italian sources disagree about which of the two premises held the roll. They agree about the gold.
suggested_refs: Villa Wanda, Arezzo, and the inventory of the search of 17 March 1981

stops.name: Rome, struck from the Grand Orient
stops.date_confidence: the expulsion is attested to the day. The parliamentary declaration and the law dissolving P2 are attested via silvio_berlusconi.journey.json at year level only; they necessarily follow the March seizure, and no day-level date was reachable.
stops.campa: On the thirty-first of October the Grande Oriente d'Italia expels him from Freemasonry, eighteen years after initiating him. Parliament goes further and declares Propaganda Due a criminal conspiracy against the constitutional order, dissolving it by law, the first time the republic has outlawed an association since the fascist parties. Neither act reaches the men on the roll, who keep their commands, their benches and their newspapers. The lodge is abolished; the list has already been printed in the newspapers.
stops.quote: Berlusconi è un uomo fuori dal comune. Ricordo bene che già allora… sapeva realizzare i suoi progetti. Un uomo del fare. Di questo c'è bisogno in Italia: non di parole, di azioni
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli to Concita De Gregorio, la Repubblica, 28 September 2003, as reproduced at disinformazione.it
suggested_refs: The 1982 law dissolving Propaganda Due and the report of the Anselmi commission
sources: disinformazione.it, la Repubblica interview of 28 September 2003

segments.name: Blackfriars, and the Wall at Champ-Dollon

stops.name: Milan, the hole in the accounts
stops.date_confidence: the collapse is attested at month level (June 1982); the stripping of Calvi's chairmanship is 17 June 1982. Day of the liquidation itself not carried here. The figure is the 1.287 billion dollars EN Wikipedia gives; a rounded 1.4 billion circulates and is not used.
stops.campa: The Bank of Italy, which has spent four years asking where the loans went, gets its answer. Banco Ambrosiano cannot account for one billion two hundred and eighty-seven million dollars, advanced to Panamanian shells the Vatican has acknowledged owning. On the seventeenth of June Calvi is stripped of the chairmanship. The bank is liquidated. It is the largest failure in the history of the Italian republic, and by the day it is announced the chairman has already left the country.
suggested_refs: The Bank of Italy inspection files on Banco Ambrosiano, 1978-1982

stops.name: London, Blackfriars Bridge
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the body was found on Friday 18 June 1982. Summaries dating this 17 June confuse it with the day the Bank of Italy removed Calvi from the chairmanship.
stops.campa: Early on the eighteenth of June a body is found hanging from scaffolding beneath Blackfriars Bridge. It is Roberto Calvi, chairman of Banco Ambrosiano until the day before yesterday, God's Banker, member of the lodge. English coroners cannot settle whether it is suicide; the first inquest says it is, the second returns an open verdict. In 2007 an Italian court will rule that he was murdered and acquit all five men tried for the murder. Gelli is investigated and never tried. The bank's money is not recovered.
suggested_refs: The two English inquests into the death of Roberto Calvi, 1982 and 1983

stops.name: Rome, Fiumicino, the suitcase with the false bottom
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level (July 1982); day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: Three weeks after London, customs at Fiumicino open a suitcase belonging to Gelli's daughter and find a false bottom packed with documents of the lodge, the Piano di rinascita democratica among them. The plan a parliamentary commission will spend years reading is recovered off an airport luggage belt. Every institution named in it, the courts, the press, the unions, the parties, is at that moment reading its own name in the papers, and the man who wrote it is outside the country and cannot be found.
suggested_refs: The Fiumicino seizure of July 1982 in the Anselmi commission's evidence

stops.name: Geneva, at the counter
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: On the thirteenth of September he walks into a Geneva bank to withdraw tens of millions of dollars from an account of the collapsed bank. The Swiss arrest him at the counter. Italy asks for him at once, and extradition proceedings begin that will run, in one form and another, for six years. He is sixty-three. He has been a fugitive for five months, his lodge has been dissolved by law, his banker is dead under a London bridge, and he has not yet been convicted of anything at all.
suggested_refs: The Swiss extradition file on Licio Gelli, 1982-1988

stops.name: Puplinge, over the wall at Champ-Dollon
stops.date_confidence: the escape is attested to the day. The prison coordinate is corrected by c. 700 m; the building straddles Puplinge and Thonex. The manner of the escape is not established in any reachable source and is not narrated here.
stops.campa: Champ-Dollon is a modern remand prison on the edge of Geneva. On the tenth of August, eleven months into his detention there, Gelli goes out of it. Switzerland has lost him out of it, and Italy, which had almost secured his extradition, will spend four years asking two continents where he is. How the escape was managed is not established in anything reachable. What is established is the date, and that he is next reported on the other side of the Atlantic.
suggested_refs: Champ-Dollon prison, canton of Geneva

stops.name: Santiago, the years no one can document
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The South American refuge is reported and the Chilean location in particular is not documented: no address, arrival date or host appears in any reachable source. The pin is central Santiago and the date a placed year within 1983-1987.
stops.campa: For four years he is in no jurisdiction that will say so. The accounts place him in South America, and in Chile in particular, ten years into a military government that dissolved its congress and outlawed its parties. Nothing reachable fixes an address, a date of arrival or a host. The Italian courts meanwhile try him without him. In Florence, in Bologna, in Rome, sentences accumulate against a man whose whereabouts no minister will state in parliament.
suggested_refs: Italian extradition requests to South American governments, 1983-1987

stops.name: Geneva, the Palais de Justice
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level (September 1987); day unknown, defaulted. Coordinate sharpened from a rounded placeholder. A detail circulating in summaries, that he was sentenced to two months in Swiss prison on surrender, is in neither Wikipedia article and is not carried.
stops.campa: He gives himself up in Geneva, to the investigating judge Jean-Pierre Trembley, in the same city and the same jurisdiction he escaped from four years earlier. He is sixty-eight and has been at liberty and unfindable for four years, and what was arranged before he walked in, and with whom, the reachable sources do not say. Swiss extradition proceedings resume from where they stopped in August 1983. This time they conclude, and this time he is guarded as if the guarding of him were a military problem.
suggested_refs: The Palais de Justice of Geneva and the Trembley investigation file

stops.name: Florence, eight years in absentia
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: Three months after the surrender a Florentine court sentences him, in his absence, to eight years for financing right-wing terrorism in Tuscany in the 1970s. He is in a Swiss cell and does not attend. Italy has now convicted him of paying for terrorist violence on its own ground, and Italy still has to ask another country's permission to put him in an Italian prison. The sentence is passed in Tuscany, thirty-five kilometres from the town he was born in and the schools that expelled him.
suggested_refs: The Florence assize judgment of 15 December 1987

stops.name: Rome, Fiumicino, brought back
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level (February 1988); day unknown, defaulted. The operational detail (about a hundred marksmen, decoy cars, a train, roadblocks, two armoured cars) reads as press description rather than record and is carried as reconstruction.
stops.campa: The extradition is executed as a military operation. The accounts describe about a hundred marksmen, decoy cars, roadblocks, a train, two armoured vehicles. The state that could not find him for four years now moves him across its own territory as though an army were coming for him. What it is guarding him against is not stated in any of the accounts. He arrives in Italy for the first time since 1982, into a country where a roll bearing nine hundred and sixty-two names has been public for seven years.
suggested_refs: The Italian security plan for the Gelli extradition, February 1988

stops.name: Bologna, acquitted of the association, convicted of the lie
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level (July 1988); day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: The Bologna court acquits him of subversive association, the charge that would have made the lodge itself the crime, and convicts him of slander: five years for the false trails laid across the station bombing investigation. The distinction holds for the rest of his life. Italian courts repeatedly find him guilty of obstructing the search for the truth about a crime, and repeatedly decline, until 2022, to find him guilty of the crime. He is sixty-nine and has been in an Italian courtroom for five months.
suggested_refs: The Bologna judgment of July 1988 on subversive association and slander

stops.name: Milan, eighteen years and six months
stops.date_confidence: attested at year level; month and day unknown, defaulted. The reduction to twelve years on appeal and the Court of Cassation's confirmation of April 1998 are both attested.
stops.campa: For the fraud that emptied Banco Ambrosiano he is sentenced in Milan to eighteen years and six months. Appeal cuts it to twelve, and in April 1998 the Court of Cassation makes the twelve definitive. He is seventy-three at sentencing and seventy-nine when it becomes final, and the Italian penal system will keep him at home on his own hill for almost every year he owes it. The bank he is convicted of looting has been dead for a decade and its chairman for as long.
suggested_refs: The Milan fraud judgment of 1992 and its appellate history

stops.name: Rome, seventeen years for the state's secrets
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level (April 1994); day unknown, defaulted. What became of this sentence on appeal is not recorded in any reachable source, an open gap.
stops.campa: In April a Roman court gives him seventeen years for divulging state secrets, an offence that requires him to have had them. The republic thereby records, in a sentence of its own courts, that a private citizen holding no post was in possession of the secrets of its intelligence services. The three men who directed those services in 1981 were on his roll. He is seventy-four, and what happens to this sentence on appeal is not recorded in anything reachable.
suggested_refs: The Piazzale Clodio judgment of April 1994 on state secrets

stops.name: Rome, the Cassation and the depistaggio
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (IT Wikipedia, 'Strage di Bologna'). This conviction is missing from most English-language chronologies. The pin is the Palazzo di Giustizia at Piazza Cavour, seat of the Court of Cassation; no source gives a venue, so the pin is institutional.
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of November the Court of Cassation sentences him definitively to ten years as a promoter of the sabotage of the Bologna investigation. Not the bomb: the burial of the bomb. For fifteen years the search for the men who killed eighty-five people in a railway station has been fed forged documents and false witnesses, and the highest court in Italy names the man who organised the feeding. It does not yet name him as the man who paid for the bomb. That comes in 2022, seven years after his death.
suggested_refs: The Cassation judgment of 23 November 1995 on the Bologna depistaggio

stops.name: Arezzo, Villa Wanda, house arrest
stops.date_confidence: attested at year level; month and day unknown, defaulted. The Nobel Prize nomination reported for the same year is reconstruction: the Nobel Committee's nomination archive is sealed for fifty years and cannot be checked before 2046.
stops.campa: He comes home to the hill above Arezzo to serve his sentences in the house where the gold was dug out of the garden. The same year he is reported nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature; he has published poems, and the nomination cannot be checked, because the committee seals its files for fifty years. He gives interviews from the villa in which he observes that the constitutional reform commission then sitting in Rome is copying his Piano di rinascita point by point, and asks for the credit.
stops.quote: Il mio Piano di rinascita? Vedo che vent'anni dopo questa Bicamerale lo sta copiando pezzo per pezzo, con la bozza Boato. Meglio tardi che mai. Mi dovrebbero almeno dare il copyright…
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, interview in Il Borghese, April 1997, cited in Marco Travaglio, 'Ad personam' (Chiarelettere, 2010), via it.wikiquote.org
suggested_refs: Villa Wanda under house arrest, 1996-1998

stops.name: The Cote d'Azur, the gold ingots
stops.date_confidence: attested at month level (September 1998); day unknown, defaulted. The town is contradicted between sources: EN Wikipedia says Cannes, IT Wikipedia says Villefranche-sur-Mer (43.7038, 7.3111), about 30 km east. The contradiction is not resolved; the pin is Cannes and the alternative is recorded here.
stops.campa: In May he goes out of the villa and is not there when the carabinieri come to look. Four months later the French police take him on the Riviera and find more than two million dollars in gold bullion in the house he is using. He is seventy-nine years old. The sources disagree about the town: the English record says Cannes, the Italian says Villefranche-sur-Mer, thirty kilometres east along the same coast. They agree about the gold, seventeen years after the ingots came out of the garden at Arezzo.
suggested_refs: The French police report on the September 1998 arrest and the bullion seizure

stops.name: Arezzo, Villa Wanda, the Repubblica interview
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The English rendering widely quoted from this interview splices two separate passages and mistranslates diritti d'autore as copyright; the Italian text reproduced at disinformazione.it is used instead.
stops.campa: Concita De Gregorio comes up the hill for la Repubblica and finds an old man at ease. Silvio Berlusconi, enrolled in the lodge in 1978, has been prime minister for two years. Gelli reads the newspapers and finds his own programme in them: the courts, the television, public order. He asks, not entirely as a joke, for the author's rights. Twenty-two years after the raid, the Piano di rinascita democratica is discussed in Italy as a description of the present and not as evidence in a criminal case.
stops.quote: Guardo il Paese, leggo i giornali e penso: ecco qua che tutto si realizza poco a poco, pezzo a pezzo. Forse sì, dovrei avere i diritti d'autore. La giustizia, la tv, l'ordine pubblico. Ho scritto tutto trent'anni fa
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli to Concita De Gregorio, la Repubblica, 28 September 2003, as reproduced in full at disinformazione.it
suggested_refs: Concita De Gregorio, la Repubblica, 28 September 2003, full text

stops.name: Rome, Piazzale Clodio, the Calvi file
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the notification; the April 2005 indictments of four others, the June 2007 acquittals and the May 2009 dismissal are attested at month level. Summaries describing Gelli as one of five indicted are not supported by the Calvi article and are not carried.
stops.campa: In April four men are indicted for the murder of Roberto Calvi, twenty-three years after Blackfriars Bridge. On the nineteenth of July Gelli is notified that he is under formal investigation. He never stands trial with them. In June 2007 the court acquits all five for insufficient evidence while ruling that Calvi was murdered and did not hang himself. In May 2009 the charges against Gelli are dropped. The murder is established in Italian law, and in Italian law it has no author.
stops.quote: Ho una vecchiaia serena. Tutte le mattine parlo con le voci della mia coscienza
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, la Repubblica interview of 28 September 2003, as rendered in Wikipedia (IT), 'Propaganda Due'
suggested_refs: The Rome prosecution file on the murder of Roberto Calvi, 2005-2009

stops.name: Pistoia, the Archivio di Stato
stops.date_confidence: attested at year level; month and day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: At eighty-seven he gives his papers to the state archive of the town he was born in: correspondence, drafts, the working record of forty years, minus one item. A register the Italians call the rubrica dei 500, a directory of five hundred, is held back and never made public. The same year he marries Gabriela Vasile. He is depositing his archive in a public institution of the republic that dissolved his lodge by law, and the republic accepts the deposit and catalogues it.
suggested_refs: The Gelli fondo at the Archivio di Stato di Pistoia, and the withheld rubrica dei 500

stops.name: Arezzo, Villa Wanda, the seizure and the end
stops.date_confidence: death attested to the day, aged 96, at the villa after transfer from the San Donato hospital. The judicial seizure of 10 October 2013 is attested to the day; the failed auctions are attested without a year, an open gap.
stops.campa: The state tries repeatedly to auction the villa to recover about a million and a half euros in trial costs from the Ambrosiano proceedings. The auctions fail and he buys his own house back. On the tenth of October 2013 it is seized again, this time over an alleged seventeen million euros in unpaid tax. On the fifteenth of December 2015, brought home from the San Donato hospital days earlier to die among his family, Licio Gelli dies in it, ninety-six years old, in a house the state owns.
stops.quote: Ci sono gli stessi uomini di vent'anni fa e non valgono nulla.
stops.quote_source: Licio Gelli, interview in L'espresso, 18 June 2010, per it.wikiquote.org
suggested_refs: The preventive seizure order on Villa Wanda, 10 October 2013

stops.name: Arezzo, Santa Maria delle Grazie
stops.date_confidence: IT Wikipedia places the Catholic funeral at Santa Maria delle Grazie in Arezzo, near the villa where the body lay in state; other summaries place the Mass at the Chiesa della Misericordia in Pistoia instead. The contradiction is not resolved. Church coordinate approximate.
stops.campa: The body lies in state at the villa. The Catholic funeral is said in the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie on the same hill, a few hundred metres from the garden the gold came out of. Relatives attend, and onlookers, and very few men of standing. A handwritten will surfaces afterwards naming a Romanian general, Bartolomeu Constantin Savoiu, Grand Master of the National Grand Lodge of Romania, as sole spiritual heir. The sources disagree about the city of the Mass, and are printed disagreeing.
suggested_refs: The Chiesa di Santa Maria delle Grazie, Viale Mecenate, Arezzo

stops.name: Pistoia, the family chapel
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, single source. Only the English-derived record names Pistoia; the Italian article's death section names no cemetery at all. No day-level date is attested and the funeral date is used as a default.
stops.campa: He is carried back to Pistoia and laid in the family chapel of the Cimitero della Misericordia, beside Wanda Vannacci, who died in 1993. Under two kilometres separate this ground from the streets where he was born ninety-six years and eight months earlier. Only one of the two languages of the record carries the burial at all: the English article names Pistoia, the Italian one names no cemetery. The town in which the kingdom expelled him from its schools at seventeen holds the grave.
suggested_refs: The Gelli family chapel, Cimitero della Misericordia, Pistoia

stops.name: Bologna, the verdict he does not hear
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the assize verdict against Paolo Bellini naming Gelli and Ortolani as mandanti and financiers; the 2020 Cavallini sentence and the appeal of 8 July 2024 upholding it are attested. Claims that this originated in 2023 investigative journalism are unsourced and are not carried.
stops.campa: Six years after his death an assize court in Bologna convicts Paolo Bellini for the station bombing and names, in its reasons, Licio Gelli and Umberto Ortolani as the men who commissioned and financed it, tracing large sums to the executors through a handwritten note of payments in Gelli's own hand. The appeal court upholds it on the eighth of July 2024. The defendant has been lying in the family chapel at Pistoia for nine years. He cannot be sentenced, and he is named.
suggested_refs: The Bologna assize judgment of 6 April 2022 and the documento Bologna
